newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reunion sees 'cash cows' for Skorpion zinc.
newsitem.headline: Reunion sees 'cash cows' for Skorpion zinc.

text.p: Reunion Mining plc would use its Zambian and Zimbabwean mines as cash cows to help fund the investigation and development of the Skorpion zinc deposit in Namibia, chairman Andrew Woollett said on Wednesday.

In an address to the Investing in African Mining Conference he said the Sanyati copper mine in Zimbabwe and the Dunrobin gold mine in Zambia were regarded as the "cash cows" that would help finance the "elephant" identified at Skorpion.
This was part of the group's strategy to develop a balanced portfolio that would fund exploration by production from smaller mines, he added.
"We have chosen to use this sort of strategy because we want to try and insulate ourselves from the vagaries of the equity market for capital raising," Woollett said.
"To some extent we designed this strategy to suit the lower risk type of investors with a European base who are unused to the way of raising money for exploration alone.
"But we are not just looking for an elephant. What we are trying to do is build a leading mining company in Africa."
Reunion has a right to earn up to a 60 percent interest in Skorpion from Erongo Mining and Exploration, a group in the Anglo American Corporation stable.
Reunion would spend $1 million on a pre-feasibility study and had made a commitment to develop the mine within three to four years.

Woollett said the pre-feasibility study on Skorpion should be completed in the first quarter of 1997, and if it was decided to do a feasibility study, this would take a year and he did not expect production to start until mid-2000.
The aim was to develop a mine that could produce not less than 75,000 tonnes a year, he said.
